result:
The one-soliton case is a useful check. A single algebraic soliton of the massive Thirring model is regular, so it should have no poles. That means any correct formula must give 0 at N = 1.

- Solutions 1 and 3 give N, which gives 1 at N = 1. That contradicts the regular one-soliton case, so they cannot be right.
- Solution 2 gives N(N+1)/2, which also gives 1 at N = 1, so it fails the same check.

My recollection of the source result is that the N-th rational solution has N(N−1)/2 poles in the upper half-plane for large |t|. This is from memory of the paper's abstract and I have not derived it here. It does give 0 at N = 1. None of the three proposed answers matches it.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
